chunks: By Allah, if you had been a visible personality and a body capable of feeling,

I would have awarded you the penalties fixed by Allah because of the people whom you deceived with desires, the communities whom you threw into destruction, the rulers whom you consigned to ruin, and drove to places of distress after which there is neither going nor returning!
Far off! Whoever stepped on your slippery place slipped, whoever rode your waves was drowned, and whoever evaded your snares received inward support,
He who keeps himself safe from you does not worry even though his affairs may be straitened and the world to him is like a day which is near expiring.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the nature of the world and its effect on those who are attached to it versus those who are safe from it?
ai.summary: In this rhetorical address to the personified World (Al-Dunya), Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs vivid imagery of slipping on its precipices and drowning in its depths to illustrate the spiritual peril of materialism. This passage, delivered to the governor of Basra, serves as a practical admonition against the allure of lavish banquets, framing worldly attachment as a deceptive snare that leads rulers and communities to ruin. The summary underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere rejection, but as a state of inner detachment where the believer remains unconcerned by external hardships, viewing the world as a transient day.
